To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) migration is a key factor in the development of education; 2) education and migration are interrelated and interdependent; and 3) migration is a powerful force in the shaping of educational policy, practice, and outcomes.
the history of education is not only a history of schools and universities, but also of other institutions and practices.
the history of education has to include the study of migrants, migration, human mobility, and the movement of ideas, practices, and policies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which migrants, migration, human mobility, and mobile lives have shaped education.
the ways that the movement of individuals, groups, and ideas across national borders and boundaries shaped the history of education in the past and continues to do so in the present.

the ways in which the history of education has been shaped by a sedentary and national bias; the ways in which a mobile history of schooling can be written by shifting the emphasis from the study of institutions to the study of people; the ways in Rethinking borders & boundaries for a mobile...  (2016).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the history of education has been too sedentary, too national, too bounded.
the mobile history of education has yet to be fully written.
the history of education needs to be written with a mobile perspective in mind.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to demonstrate the ways in which migrants have contributed to education and schooling in a variety of ways and across different historical contexts.
the papers in this special issue demonstrate that the history of education is a mobile history and that the history of migration is an educational history.
it is about the ways in which people move, the reasons for which they move, and the consequences for their education.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of migration can be an effective way to reframe and reorientate the history of education, and that this is a task of both conceptual and empirical importance.
the history of education needs to be rethought in order to accommodate the mobility of people, ideas, and institutions.
the history of education is a history of mobility and migration.
